title: Why preservatives appear
expanded_text: Preservatives are used to slow spoilage quality loss or microbial growth. The exact role depends on the ingredient and food type.

title: Why emulsifiers appear
expanded_text: Emulsifiers help ingredients that normally separate such as oil and water remain evenly distributed. They can improve creaminess softness and shelf stability.

title: Why thickeners appear
expanded_text: Thickeners gums and starches change how a food flows gels or holds particles in suspension. Small amounts can have a large texture effect.

title: Why acids appear
short_text: Food acids add tartness and balance pH.
expanded_text: Acidulants such as citric malic lactic and acetic acid create sourness and help foods keep a consistent acidity profile.

title: Why colors appear
expanded_text: Color ingredients may make food more visually consistent replace color lost in processing or create a specific brand appearance.

title: Why sweeteners appear
short_text: Sweeteners provide sweetness in different ways.
expanded_text: Some sweeteners add sugar and bulk while high-intensity sweeteners add sweetness with little bulk. Sugar alcohols sit between those categories.

title: Why leaveners appear
expanded_text: Leavening ingredients help create air pockets or lift in baked goods. They can affect texture browning and flavor.

title: Allergen badge
short_text: This item may matter for people avoiding a specific allergen.
expanded_text: Allergen badges should preserve the exact matched ingredient and show the relevant allergen family such as milk egg soy wheat peanut tree nut fish shellfish sesame mustard or sulfites.

title: Gluten context
short_text: Gluten and wheat are related but not identical filters.
expanded_text: Wheat allergy and gluten avoidance should be shown separately when possible because an ingredient can be relevant to one or both concerns.

title: Jurisdiction note
expanded_text: Food additive names permissions and warning requirements can vary by country. The app should avoid universal claims unless the jurisdiction is known.

title: Unknown ingredient term
short_text: The scanner did not recognize this term yet.
expanded_text: Unknown terms should be saved with the original OCR text so they can improve the alias database and matching model over time.

title: Low-confidence OCR match
short_text: The scanner may have misread this term.
expanded_text: Low-confidence matches should show both the original text and the suggested ingredient so the user can correct it.

title: Reviewed content
short_text: This entry is ready for general app display.
expanded_text: Reviewed content means the row has stable educational wording and does not make unsupported medical claims.

title: Draft content
short_text: This entry is useful but not final.
expanded_text: Draft content can support matching and general education but should avoid strong safety regulatory or medical statements.

title: Source-backed content needed
short_text: This entry needs authoritative backing before strong claims are shown.
expanded_text: Rows requiring source support should remain in the database for matching but should show neutral function notes until citations are added.
